what: the day's ranked clusters, in the desk's own one line, sources counted and linked (Jack, 5 October 2026)
what_a_wire_line_is: Each line is the desk's own one-line summary of a story it ranked, with its sources counted and linked. It is not a story the desk wrote or checked; only the item with a badge was checked.

items.line: Deutsche Bank to launch Bitcoin and Ethereum custody for institutional clients within weeks, targeting Asia expansion in 2027.

items.line: Federal judge denied joint Gemini-CFTC motion to void $5M settlement, holding that policy changes do not reopen voluntary settlements.

items.line: Mizuho, MUFG and SMBC completed July yen stablecoin pilot covering issuance, transfer and redemption; real transactions targeted for fiscal 2026.

items.line: Bank of Russia confirmed ban on peer-to-peer Bitcoin trading, effective July 1, 2027; all trades must route through approved brokers or exchanges.
titles: Russia Will Soon Ban Peer-to-Peer Bitcoin Trading, Central Bank Confirms

items.line: Australia released draft bill to adopt OECD's Common Crypto Asset Reporting Framework; first international tax data exchanges due 2028.
titles: Australia releases draft bill to adopt OECD crypto tax reporting framework

checked.says: Bitcoin Magazine reports Deutsche Bank is 'just weeks away' from launching crypto custody for European institutional clients and plans to expand to Asia, with the German lender's corporate banking chief quoted by Reuters.
checked.unconfirmed: The specific custody assets (Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDC, EURC) are confirmed only in U.Today; the 'within weeks' timeline appears in multiple sources but rests primarily on the Reuters quote relayed by Bitcoin Magazine and U.Today.
